transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Samir (Redwood Product), James (Aurora CTO), Priya (Aurora Head of ML), Diego (Aurora SecOps), Emma (Aurora SRE)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to align on POC success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan and decision criteria between Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployment modes. Security and networking questions were raised; Redwood to provide security docs and benchmark runbook. POC target window: 2-4 weeks after benchmark signoff.

Transcribed conversation:
00:00 - Maya: Hey folks, thanks for joining. we wanted to run through the POC scope for Aurora. basically figure out success criteria, the workloads, and which deployment mode we should plan for — hosted, dedicated, or private.
00:22 - James: Yep, thanks. We had a quick internal chat, high level our priorities are latency under 150ms p95 for short chat flows, cost per 1k tokens that is comparable or better than what we're seeing now, and data residency / encryption requirements for some PHI-like traces.
00:40 - Priya: Also want to make sure quality is consistent — hallucination rate for our summarization task must be under 1% on a measured eval set.
01:05 - Ethan: ok, that's helpful. A couple clarifying q's: what's your expected peak QPS and avg tokens per request? that drives whether Hosted continuous batching or Dedicated pools make sense.
01:22 - Emma: Right now our internal tests have about 12 QPS steady, peaks to 45 QPS for some campaigns. Avg token length is ~220 tokens, with some longer 1k token recs.
01:40 - Samir: 45 QPS with 220 avg tokens is a decent mid-sized workload — we can run baseline hosted tests first; dedicated starts to make more sense as you push for predictable tail latency and cost at scale.
02:03 - Diego: On security: we need SAML SSO, audit logs for every request, KMS integration for key management, and ideally an option to do Private inside our VPC or on-prem for regulated traces. any immediate blockers?
02:30 - Maya: We support SAML and RBAC in the console, full audit logging, and KMS integrations. For Private, we have a VPC/private deployment option with customer-managed keys and HSM support, though that'll add setup time. We'll send the SOC2 and architecture docs after this call.
03:05 - Priya: For POC success criteria — suggestion: agree on latency SLOs (p95), a quality eval suite (we'll provide), and a cost-per-1k-token baseline. if hosted meets latency and cost targets, we may not need Dedicated/Private initially.
03:30 - Ethan: Totally. Practically our POC approach is: (1) baseline hosted run with your sample workload; (2) if tail latency or cost is off, we spin up a Dedicated pool with reserved GPUs and run the same benchmarks; (3) as a last step we demo Private in a controlled environment if data residency requires it. this keeps the timeline short.
04:00 - James: Timeline? how long for each step?
04:12 - Maya: Baseline hosted run typically 1-2 days to run and analyze if we have your sample corpus. The Dedicated config and benchmark maybe 3-5 days to provision and run. Private evaluation depends on connectivity and legal — could be 2-4 weeks to set up a private control plane or on-prem package. so overall POC 2-4 weeks depending on chosen scope.
04:40 - Emma: For network, our security team prefers minimal inbound rules; can we do outbound-only peering?
04:55 - Ethan: For Hosted, outbound-only from your VPC to Redwood endpoints works. For Private we do VPC peering or private link; if you need air-gapped on-prem we'll need a deployment window and access plan.
05:25 - Priya: Benchmarks — what metrics will you capture?
05:30 - Ethan: We collect p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost estimate, and quality metrics tied to your eval set. Also KV cache hit rates for prefix-heavy flows. We'll provide a runbook template.
06:15 - James: About cost — how do batching and quantization recommendations factor?
06:24 - Samir: We'll propose batching windows and quant profiles; quantization can reduce cost but sometimes affects quality. Our Optimize module will recommend quant profiles based on your eval and we can run ablation to show trade-offs.
06:45 - Diego: Any limitations on model choices? we need specific family of models for our internal eval.
07:00 - Ethan: We support a model catalog; for POC we can test with a couple of open models plus Redwood-verified variants. if you have a proprietary model we can load a checkpoint for Dedicated or Private.
07:20 - Priya: Ok, for quality testing we'll share a labeled eval set of 2k examples and a production sample of 5k prompts.
07:35 - Maya: perfect — that will let us compute hallucination rates and cost per inference.
08:00 - Emma: about SLOs — can Redwood provide per-route SLOs and tracing hooks so our SREs can alert on degradations?
08:12 - Lena: Yes, Console has per-route dashboards, traces, and can emit alerts. we can export traces to your telemetry stack.
08:30 - Diego: We need to confirm data retention and logs retention policy for Hosted. our compliance needs a 90-day retention and ability to purge specific tenants.
08:45 - Maya: Hosted supports configurable retention; enterprise plans include longer retention windows and purge APIs. We'll include details in the security pack.
09:05 - James: Decision criteria recap — if Hosted meets p95 <150ms, cost <X (to be defined with your cost target), and passes security check then we go Hosted. If p95 is okay but tail spikes or cost is high, Dedicated. If any regulatory or residency block, Private.
09:30 - Priya: Also include operational friction — how much infra work we need. Hosted minimal, Dedicated needs reserved capacity integration, Private will require our infra team engagement.
09:50 - Ethan: Agreed. Also note fallbacks — we can route to a cheaper model variant during bursts to keep availability.
10:05 - Samir: On benchmarking specifics — we'll run mixes: chat-like flows (220 tokens), long-reads (1k tokens), embeddings batch job (50k vectors). each needs different perf characteristics.
10:30 - Maya: Good to include embeddings cost/throughput as well; that often drives Dedicated decisions when you have high embed volumes.
11:00 - James: Ok, let's talk initial numbers: we'll target a hosted benchmark at 20 QPS steady, 60 QPS peak, 220 avg tokens; latency target p95 150ms. if Hosted cost per 1k tokens is within 20% of our target we'll consider it.
11:25 - Ethan: Noted. We'll run simulated traffic with synthetic bursts to reproduce peak.
11:40 - Priya: For the POC evaluation, can Redwood help run A/B comparisons vs our current provider?
11:50 - Maya: Yes, we can run side-by-side benchmarks, and we can share the CSV with latency/cost/quality metrics.
12:10 - Diego: Legal/procurement — we'll need a basic SLAs summary and data processing agreement to review.
12:20 - Maya: We'll attach a standard SOW template and the SLA summary in the follow-up.
12:35 - James: Who will own the benchmark coordination on Redwood side?
12:40 - Lena: Lena will coordinate scheduling, Ethan will lead the technical runs, and Maya will handle commercial and security docs.
12:55 - Maya: summary and next steps: Redwood sends security pack + SOC2 by Feb 3, Redwood sends benchmark runbook and config by Feb 5, Aurora shares sample corpus and QPS targets by Feb 4, schedule a 2-hour live benchmark week of Feb 10.
13:15 - James: sounds good. any open questions?
13:22 - Priya: one minor — can you support customer-managed KMS keys for Hosted?
13:30 - Samir: Hosted enterprise tier supports bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS integrations; we'll document the flow.
13:45 - Diego: ok that's it from SecOps.
13:52 - Maya: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with attachments and calendar invite for the benchmark.
13:58 - James: thanks, talk soon.
14:02 - [call ends]

References mentioned:
- Benchmarks/runbook (Redwood to attach)
- SOC2 report, ISO docs, data processing agreement (DPA)
- Example eval set and sample prompts (Aurora to provide)

End of transcript.
